trip.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson opens the section on MVD records, changes and the road test, starting with money and time. First, a fee rule worth knowing early. If MVD revokes, suspends or cancels your license, you may owe a fresh application fee in addition to a reinstatement fee. Second, a habit that can spare you a wasted drive. To save time, check AZMVDNow.gov first to see whether your transaction can be finished online, and use it to fill out an application for an ID, driver license or title. In the rest of this lesson we will add the other fees the manual lists, the ways to pay, what the portal can book for you, and the days when offices are most crowded.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":48,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Two charges, not one","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"A fresh application fee may apply.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"The reinstatement fee applies too.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"Plan for both.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the fee rule in plain terms. If MVD revokes, suspends or cancels your license, you may owe a fresh application fee in addition to a reinstatement fee. The manual repeats the same idea as a warning in another place. A revoked, suspended or canceled license can cost two charges, a new application fee plus a reinstatement fee, not just one reinstatement fee. So when you hear that a license was revoked, suspended or canceled, picture two separate charges on the bill. The reinstatement fee is the one people expect. The fresh application fee is the one they forget, and it is the one this rule is really about.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Other fees and paying","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Abandoned vehicle fee is higher on federal land.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-F08"]},{"text":"A returned check has its own fee.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-F08"]},{"text":"Pay by cash, card, cashier's check or money order.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"MVD lists a five hundred dollar fee for an abandoned vehicle. That fee rises to six hundred dollars when the vehicle is left on federal land, and a check that comes back unpaid carries its own twenty-five dollar charge. Now for how you pay. Besides cash, most MVD fees can be paid by credit card, cashier's check or money order, and checks or money orders should be made out to Motor Vehicle Division. Keep the payee name exactly as written when you fill out a check or money order. If you are unsure which payment to use, cash, credit card, cashier's check and money order all appear on the manual's list for most fees.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Busy days to avoid","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"First two and last two days are busiest.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F04"]},{"text":"The day after a holiday is busy too.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F04"]},{"text":"Second Wednesday: most offices closed until noon.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap many people walk into. They pick the first free day of the month to visit, and the office is packed. Offices are busiest on the first two and last two days of each month and on the day after a holiday, and most offices stay closed until noon on the second Wednesday of every month. The portal also handles bookings, which can spare you a wait. AZMVDNow.gov is also where you book an appointment for a road test, a Travel credential or a license renewal. So plan around the crowded days and the late Wednesday opening, and book ahead where you can.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the fee rule","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Your license was suspended.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"Which fees may you owe?","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: your license was suspended, and you are ready to get it back. Which fees may you owe? Picture the bill before you look at the answer. The answer is a fresh application fee and a reinstatement fee. If MVD revokes, suspends or cancels your license, you may owe a fresh application fee in addition to a reinstatement fee. If you answered only the reinstatement fee, that is the most common slip. A revoked, suspended or canceled license can cost two charges, a new application fee plus a reinstatement fee, not just one reinstatement fee. Keep both charges on your list whenever a license was revoked, suspended or canceled.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Fees and services recap","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F08","sec01-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two possible charges after losing a license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F08","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"Check the portal, book ahead, avoid busy days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F08","sec01-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close this lesson, bring the pieces together. A license that was revoked, suspended or canceled may cost a fresh application fee on top of the reinstatement fee. MVD also lists separate fees for an abandoned vehicle and for a returned check, and most fees can be paid several ways, with checks made out to Motor Vehicle Division. Check the online portal before any visit, use it to book road tests, Travel credentials and renewals, and avoid the first two and last two days of the month, the day after a holiday, and the second Wednesday morning.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F08","sec01-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u02","module_id":"sec01-m02","objective_ids":["sec01-u02"],"title":{"text":"Identification and legal presence","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-R05"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Bringing the right papers the first time keeps an MVD visit short, and an out-of-state license can even waive a test.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07"]},{"text":"Legal presence decides whether MVD may issue or renew a license at all.","fact_ids":["sec01-F23","sec01-R09"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Luis moves to Arizona with a license from another state and his car's out-of-state title and plates.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07"]},"reasoning":{"text":"He brings the required identification, his old license, the title, registration and plates, and has the vehicle identification number ready.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-R05"]},"result":{"text":"His old license serves as secondary identification and can waive the written or road test.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking an out-of-state license is all the identification you need.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"It works as secondary identification, so you still bring the required identification as well.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Old license helps, but bring everything.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A newcomer brings only an out-of-state license to MVD. What is missing?","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]},"answer":{"text":"The required identification.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05"]},"rationale":{"text":"The out-of-state license is secondary identification and may waive a test, but the required identification is still needed.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"What to bring to MVD","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Your out-of-state license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},{"text":"Required identification and vehicle papers.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},{"text":"Proof of legal presence.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson is about what to carry into an MVD office and the identity rules behind it. Start with one helpful document. Bring your out-of-state driver license to MVD, because it serves as a secondary form of identification and can waive the written or road test. Then we will cover the rest of the list, the legal presence rule that applies when a license is issued and when it is renewed, and a short warning MVD gives about its identification rules. Watch for the difference between a document that helps and a document that is required.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The visit checklist","fact_ids":["sec01-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Required identification.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07"]},{"text":"Out-of-state title, registration and plates.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07"]},{"text":"Vehicle identification number ready.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the full list for a visit. When visiting MVD, bring your required identification, any out-of-state title, registration and license plates, and have the vehicle identification number (VIN) ready. Notice that the list mixes items about you and items about your vehicle. Your identification proves who you are. The title, registration, plates and the vehicle identification number are about the car you are bringing into the state. Having the number ready, rather than looking for it at the counter, is part of the instruction itself.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Helpful is not required","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"An old license is secondary identification.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]},{"text":"It can waive the written or road test.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]},{"text":"Required identification still comes too.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"This is the trap in this lesson. Because an out-of-state license can waive a test, some people assume it can stand in for everything else. It cannot. An out-of-state license brought to MVD works as secondary identification and may waive the written or road test, and you still bring the required identification as well. So treat the old license as a bonus, never as a replacement. Bring it along with the required identification, and you get the help it offers without being turned away. In short, the out-of-state license is secondary identification, and secondary means it comes in addition to the required identification.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Legal presence rule","fact_ids":["sec01-F23","sec01-R09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Proof that federal law authorizes your presence.","fact_ids":["sec01-F23","sec01-R09"]},{"text":"Needed to issue a license or ID.","fact_ids":["sec01-F23","sec01-R09"]},{"text":"Needed to renew one too.","fact_ids":["sec01-F23","sec01-R09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Arizona law sets a firm gate here. Under a section of the Arizona Revised Statutes, MVD may not issue or renew a driver license or ID card unless the applicant proves that federal law authorizes their presence in the United States. The manual stresses the renewal part on purpose. Legal presence is a gate for both issuing and renewing a license or ID card, not only for a first license. So the same proof matters at your first visit and again every time you renew. Keep the words issue and renew side by side in your memory, because the rule covers both of them.","fact_ids":["sec01-F23","sec01-R09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Rules that can change","fact_ids":["sec01-F24","sec01-F23"]},"lines":[{"text":"MVD may change identification rules.","fact_ids":["sec01-F24","sec01-F23"]},{"text":"No advance notice is promised.","fact_ids":["sec01-F24","sec01-F23"]},{"text":"Check before you go.","fact_ids":["sec01-F24","sec01-F23"]}],"narration":{"text":"One more line from the manual is short but important. MVD warns that identification requirements can change without notice. That is why the earlier habit of checking before you go matters for documents too. A list you remember from a friend's visit may no longer match what MVD asks for today. Pair this warning with the legal presence rule: the proof itself is required, but the details of what counts can change. Under Arizona Revised Statutes section twenty-eight-three thousand one hundred fifty-three(D), MVD may not issue or renew a driver license or ID card unless the applicant proves that federal law authorizes their presence in the United States.","fact_ids":["sec01-F24","sec01-F23"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the document rule","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"A newcomer brings only an old license.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]},{"text":"What else is needed?","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a newcomer walks into MVD carrying only a license from another state. What is still missing? The answer is the required identification. An out-of-state license brought to MVD works as secondary identification and may waive the written or road test, and you still bring the required identification as well. The old license still earns its place in the bag, because it can do two useful things. Bring your out-of-state driver license to MVD, because it serves as a secondary form of identification and can waive the written or road test. Keep both ideas together: helpful document, plus required identification.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Identification recap","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-R05","sec01-F23","sec01-R09","sec01-F24"]},"lines":[{"text":"Bring your old license and the required identification.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-R05","sec01-F23","sec01-R09","sec01-F24"]},{"text":"Have vehicle papers and the vehicle number ready.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-R05","sec01-F23","sec01-R09","sec01-F24"]},{"text":"Legal presence is checked at issue and renewal.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-R05","sec01-F23","sec01-R09","sec01-F24"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, bring your out-of-state license, because it counts as secondary identification and can waive the written or road test, but also bring the required identification. For a vehicle from another state, bring its title, registration and plates, and have the vehicle identification number ready. MVD may not issue or renew a license or ID card without proof that federal law authorizes your presence, and that proof matters at every renewal. Finally, remember that identification requirements can change without notice.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-R05","sec01-F23","sec01-R09","sec01-F24"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":32,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u03","module_id":"sec01-m03","objective_ids":["sec01-u03"],"title":{"text":"Reporting name and address changes","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-R01","sec01-F10"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Reporting changes on time keeps renewal notices and other mail reaching you and avoids a possible citation.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]},{"text":"Knowing which change can be done online saves an unneeded office visit.","fact_ids":["sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Priya moves across town and marries in the same month, so both her address and her name change.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-R01"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Both must reach MVD within ten days; she files the address online and takes identification in both names to an office for the name change.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-R02"]},"result":{"text":"To have the new name and address printed, she applies for a replacement license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F15"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a name change has a longer reporting window than an address change.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"Both changes share one ten-day deadline.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F09"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Ten days for either change.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-R01"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Someone changed their name two weeks ago and has not told MVD. Are they on time?","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F09"]},"answer":{"text":"No, both name and address changes are due within ten days.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01"]},"rationale":{"text":"Arizona law sets one ten-day deadline for a change of name or address.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-R01"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Telling MVD about changes","fact_ids":["sec01-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"One deadline for name and address.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Different ways to file each.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09"]},{"text":"A new card is a separate step.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers what to do when your name or your address changes. Start with the deadline, because everything else hangs on it. Arizona law requires you to tell MVD about any change of name or address within ten days. Then we will look at what can go wrong if you skip the report, how an address change is filed, how a name change is filed, which records update by themselves, and why your plastic card does not change on its own. Each of these steps has its own rule, so we will take them one at a time and then put them together at the end.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Why reporting matters","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Mail may stop reaching you.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Police may cite you.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Ten days is the limit.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is what the manual says can happen if you do not report a change. If you skip reporting a change, renewal notices and other mail about your license or vehicles may never reach you, and police may cite you. The first problem is practical: notices about your license or vehicles go to the old address. The second is a legal risk, because police may cite you. Both follow from missing the deadline you just learned, so the safest habit is to report a change as soon as it happens. Remember that the ten-day rule covers a change of name as well as a change of address.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Filing an address change","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-F13","sec01-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"File online with your details.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-F13","sec01-F12"]},{"text":"One change updates linked records.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-F13","sec01-F12"]},{"text":"Your card keeps the old address.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-F13","sec01-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"An address change can be filed online. You give your full name, the new address with zip code, your license number and birth date, plus the final four digits of your Social Security number. Because MVD links all of your records, one address change updates your license or ID record and every vehicle record that lists you as first registered owner. One thing does not change, though. Reporting a new address does not reprint your card; to show the new address on the credential you must apply for and buy a replacement license. So a single filing updates the records, and a replacement license is a second, separate step if you want the new address on the card.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-F13","sec01-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":47,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Records change, card does not","fact_ids":["sec01-R03","sec01-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Filing updates MVD records.","fact_ids":["sec01-R03","sec01-F12"]},{"text":"The printed card stays the same.","fact_ids":["sec01-R03","sec01-F12"]},{"text":"Buy a replacement to reprint it.","fact_ids":["sec01-R03","sec01-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"This is the most common surprise in this lesson. People file an address change and expect the card in their wallet to match. Filing an address change updates MVD records but leaves the old address on your card until you buy a replacement license. Nothing is wrong when the old address is still printed. The record is correct, and the card simply has not been replaced. If you want the card to show the new address, apply for and buy a replacement license. In other words, filing the change and reprinting the card are two separate actions, and only the second one changes what is printed on your license.","fact_ids":["sec01-R03","sec01-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Filing a name change","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Done in person at an office.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"Bring identification in both names.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"Names must match Social Security records.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"A name change works differently. A name change is done in person at any MVD office or at an authorized third party office that handles driver licenses, with identification in both your new and your former name. Printing the new name is its own step. To have the new name printed on your license you apply for a replacement license, and every name must be verifiable against Social Security Administration records. Compare this with the address change you just learned. An address change can be done entirely online, while the manual sends a name change to an MVD or authorized third party office with identification in both names. So the address can be handled from home, while the name change needs an office visit and identification in both names.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":52,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the deadline","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"A name changed two weeks ago.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Is the report on time?","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: someone changed their name two weeks ago and still has not told MVD. Is that on time? Think it through before the answer. No, it is late. Name changes and address changes share one deadline in Arizona: both must reach MVD within ten days, so there is no separate longer window for a name change. The rule behind it applies to both kinds of change. Arizona law requires you to tell MVD about any change of name or address within ten days.
